newsitem.title: USA: US Gulf grain facility still shut following crash.
newsitem.headline: US Gulf grain facility still shut following crash.

text.p: A Zen-Noh Grain Corp grain loading facility near the Gulf of Mexico remained closed Monday following a vessel crash that occurred Thursday, a company official said.

"As of this morning, we're still reviewing our options and timetables right now," said Kevin Adams, merchandising manager from Zen-Noh in Mandeville, La. "We don't expect to have any good answers until the end of next week," he said.
The facility in Convent, La. on the Mississippi River was damaged when a ship loading corn destined for Saudi Arabia struck one of four ship loading towers.
Ship loading towers are the mechanisms used to deliver grain from the elevator to the vessel, Adams said.
Adams would not comment on whether the company planned to re-route stalled shipments of grain.
The Zen-Noh facility has an annual capacity of 400 million to 500 million bushels and is one of the largest at the U.S. port, Adams said. ((Anna Driver 312-983-7294))
